title: Week 6 Analysis
subtitle: Everybody lost points. Cadegn's lead is down to 10.
intro_paragraphs: For the second time this season (the first was Week 3), every bettor's total went down. Four divisions reshuffled, and almost none of the moves matched anyone's picks. The biggest hit came in the AFC North, where Cleveland, Pittsburgh, and Baltimore are all 4-2 and the tiebreakers put them in a different order than last week.
Six teams have played five games instead of six: Carolina and Kansas City had their byes in Week 5, and Minnesota, Detroit, Miami, and Cincinnati were off this week.

fun_facts.heading: The AFC North Wiped Out Everyone
fun_facts.body: Nobody has a single exact hit left in the AFC North. Last week the Steelers in third paid all seven bettors, and the Ravens in first paid Mike T, Dustin, and Tom too. Now it's Browns, Steelers, Ravens, Bengals, with the top three all 4-2 and Cincinnati at 3-2 after its bye. Mike T, Dustin, and Tom each lost 6 there, and everyone else lost 3. Every bettor picked the Browns to finish last, and they're in first.

fun_facts.heading: Cadegn Still Leads, by 10
fun_facts.body: Cadegn fell 9 points to 56: 3 in the AFC North, 3 in the NFC South when New Orleans climbed out of last, and 3 in the NFC West when Arizona did the same. It's the first time Cadegn's total has gone down since Week 3, and the lead over 2nd is down from 13 to 10. Both of Cadegn's perfect divisions, the AFC East and NFC East, held for another week.

fun_facts.heading: Mike T Holds 2nd Alone
fun_facts.body: Mike T lost 6 to finish at 46 but now has 2nd to himself. The Bears moving into third in the NFC North matched Mike T's pick and got back 3 of the points lost elsewhere. Dustin had the same Week 6 (-6, with the same Bears pick) and is at 43, tied on points with Hume. Hume is ranked ahead on the second tiebreaker, two top-2 bonuses to Dustin's one. Hume lost 9 because the Bears move also knocked out Hume's Bears-in-last pick. Tom also lost 9 and is 5th at 42, so 3rd through 5th are separated by one point.

fun_facts.heading: Farmer Falls Further Behind
fun_facts.body: Farmer lost 9 to drop to 21, 10 behind Dilger and 35 behind the lead. The Saints climbing out of last in the NFC South cost Farmer 3 points that the Saints falling to last had given them the week before. Farmer is still the only bettor without a perfect division. Dilger lost 6 and is 6th at 31.

fun_facts.heading: The Locks: Down to the AFC East
fun_facts.body:
Only 2 of the 8 preseason unanimous picks are holding, down from 4: the Bills first and the Patriots second in the AFC East. Buffalo is 6 for 6. The Steelers in third broke when Pittsburgh moved up to second, and the Cardinals in last broke when Arizona passed the Rams.

That leaves the Rams, the pool's unanimous pick to win the NFC West, in last place at 2-4 while the 49ers are 6-0.

fun_facts.heading: Division-Winner Picks Got Worse
fun_facts.body: With Cleveland back in first, four divisions are led by teams nobody in the pool picked to win: the Browns, Vikings, Panthers, and 49ers. Cadegn is the only bettor still at 3 of 8 division-winner picks currently correct (Jaguars, Bills, Giants). Mike T, Hume, and Farmer are at 2 of 8, and Dilger, Dustin, and Tom are down to 1, the Bills.

closing_paragraph: A week where everybody lost points still left the order mostly in place. Cadegn leads by 10, and 3rd through 5th are covered by one point. The AFC North has three teams at 4-2, so it could reshuffle again next week. Same time next Tuesday.
